tagline: South through farm country to the lakes once blamed on meteors.
intro: The byway picks up NC 242 at US 421, a few miles south of Spivey's Corner, and runs south through Salemburg and Roseboro, across the southeastern tip of Cumberland County and down into Bladen to Elizabethtown, near the Cape Fear River. It is farm country most of the way, and the farmland owes something to the lakes.

Those lakes are Carolina bays, oval hollows in the coastal plain, many of them lined up northwest to southeast. People long blamed them on meteors. Geologists now favor wind and water, and the meteors have been dismissed for want of evidence, starting with a crater.

moments.title: Spivey's Corner
moments.text: From 1969 until 2015 this crossroads, a few miles north of the byway's start, held the National Hollerin' Contest, reviving the old art of calling across long distances before there were telephones.

moments.title: Jones Lake State Park
moments.text: Jones Lake has no stream to feed it and lives on rain alone, and its neighbor, Salters Lake, is named for the woman who spied on the Tory camp at Elizabethtown.

moments.title: Elizabethtown
moments.text: In August 1781 the Patriots waded the Cape Fear by night, attacked with Washington's name for a battle cry, and drove the Loyalists into a ravine by the river still called Tory Hole.
